metadata.title: A Differential Equation for Modeling Nesterov's Accelerated Gradient Method: Theory and Insights

nodes.name: Convex minimization
nodes.statement: In the simplest and most standard form, we are interested in solving \[\mbox{minimize}\quad f(x),\] where $f$ is a convex function, smooth or non-smooth, and $x \in \R^n$ is the variable.

nodes.name: Composite optimization
nodes.section: Appendix C. ODE for Composite Optimization
nodes.statement: we develop an ODE for composite optimization, \begin{equation} \mbox{minimize} \quad f(x) = g(x) + h(x), \end{equation} where $g\in \mathcal{F}_{L}$ and $h$ is a general convex function possibly taking on the value $+ \infty$.

nodes.name: Nesterov's accelerated gradient method (Nesterov's scheme)
nodes.statement: starting with $x_0$ and $y_0 = x_0$, inductively define \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} & x_k = y_{k-1} - s\nabla f(y_{k-1})\\ & y_k = x_k + \frac{k-1}{k+2} (x_k - x_{k-1}). \end{aligned} \end{equation}

nodes.name: The ODE modeling Nesterov's scheme
nodes.statement: This ODE takes the following form: \begin{equation} \ddot{X} + \frac{3}{t}\dot{X} + \nabla f(X) = 0 \end{equation} for $t > 0$, with initial conditions $X(0) = x_0, \der{X}(0) = 0$

nodes.name: Generalized ODE parameterized by $r$
nodes.statement: \begin{equation} \ddot{X} + \frac{r}{t}\dot{X} + \nabla f(X) = 0 \end{equation} with initial conditions $X(0) = x_0, \dot X(0) = 0$.

nodes.name: Generalized Nesterov's scheme
nodes.statement: we propose the generalized Nesterov's scheme, \begin{gather} \begin{aligned} &x_k = y_{k-1} -  sG_s(y_{k-1})\\ &y_k = x_k + \frac{k-1}{k+r-1}(x_k -x_{k-1}), \end{aligned} \end{gather} starting from $y_0 = x_0$.

nodes.name: Speed restarted ODE
nodes.statement: The speed restarted ODE is thus \begin{equation} \ddot X(t) + \frac{3}{\tsr}\dot X(t) + \nabla f(X(t)) = 0, \end{equation} where $\tsr$ is set to zero whenever $\langle \dot X, \ddot X\rangle = 0$ and between two consecutive restarts, $\tsr$ grows just as $t$. That is, $\tsr = t - \tau$, where $\tau$ is the latest restart time. In particular, $\tsr = 0$ at $t = 0$.

nodes.name: Directional subgradient
nodes.section: Appendix C. ODE for Composite Optimization
nodes.statement: A Borel measurable function $G(x, p;f)$ defined on $\mathbb{R}^n\times \mathbb{R}^{n}$ is said to be a directional subgradient of $f$ if \begin{align*} &G(x, p) \in \partial f(x),\\ & \langle G(x, p), p\rangle = \sup_{\xi\in \partial f(x)}\langle \xi, p \rangle \end{align*} for all $x, p$.

nodes.name: Speed restarting time
nodes.statement: For the ODE \eqref{key}, we call \begin{equation} T = T(x_0; f) = \sup \left\{t > 0: \forall u\in (0, t), ~ \frac{\d\norm{\dot X(u)}^2}{\d u} > 0 \right\} \end{equation} the speed restarting time. In words, $T$ is the first time the velocity $\|\dot X\|$ decreases.

nodes.name: Existence and uniqueness of the ODE solution (regularity)
conclusions: the ODE \eqref{key} ... has a \textit{unique global} solution $X\in C^{2}((0,\infty);\R^n)\cap C^{1}([0,\infty);\R^n)$
nodes.statement: For any $f\in\mathcal{F}_{\infty} :=  \cup_{L > 0}\mathcal{F}_L$ and any $x_0\in\R^n$, the ODE \eqref{key} with initial conditions $X(0) = x_0, \der{X}(0) = 0$ has a \textit{unique global} solution $X\in C^{2}((0,\infty);\R^n)\cap C^{1}([0,\infty);\R^n)$.

nodes.name: Nesterov's scheme converges to the ODE
nodes.statement: For any $f \in \mathcal{F}_{\infty}$, as the step size $s \goto 0$, Nesterov's scheme \eqref{eq:nesterov-scheme} converges to the ODE \eqref{key} in the sense that for all fixed $T > 0$, \[ \lim_{s\goto 0}\max_{0 \le k \le \frac{T}{\sqrt{s}}}\left\| x_k - X\left( k\sqrt{s} \right) \right\| = 0. \]

nodes.name: Inverse quadratic convergence rate of the ODE
assumptions: let $X(t)$ be the unique global solution to \eqref{key} with initial conditions $X(0) = x_0, \dot X(0) = 0$
nodes.statement: For any $f\in\mathcal{F}_{\infty}$, let $X(t)$ be the unique global solution to \eqref{key} with initial conditions $X(0) = x_0, \dot X(0) = 0$. Then, for any $t > 0$, \begin{equation} f(X(t)) - f^\star \le \frac{2\norm{x_0-x^\star}^2}{t^2}. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Oscillation: spacing of roots of $X(t)-x^\star$
nodes.statement: Denote by $0 < t_1 < t_2 < \cdots $ all the roots of $X(t) - x^\star$. Then these roots satisfy, for all $i \ge 1$, \begin{equation} t_1 < \frac{7.6635}{\sqrt{\mu}}, ~ t_{i+1} - t_{i} < \frac{7.6635}{\sqrt{\mu}}, ~ t_{i+2} - t_i > \frac{\pi}{\sqrt{L}}. \end{equation}

nodes.name: High friction convergence rate ($r>3$)
nodes.statement: The solution $X$ to \eqref{eq:ode_r} satisfies \begin{equation} f(X(t)) - f^\star \le \frac{(r-1)^2\|x_0 - x^\star\|^2}{2t^2}, \quad \int^{\infty}_0 t(f(X(t))-f^\star)\d t \le \frac{(r-1)^2\|x_0 - x^\star\|^2}{2(r-3)}. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Discrete high friction convergence rate
assumptions: The sequence $\{x_k\}$ given by \eqref{eq:nesterov_general} with $0 < s \le 1/L$
nodes.statement: The sequence $\{x_k\}$ given by \eqref{eq:nesterov_general} with $0 < s \le 1/L$ satisfies \begin{equation} f(x_k) - f^\star \le \frac{(r-1)^2\|x_0 - x^\star\|^2}{2s(k+r-2)^2}, \quad \sum_{k=1}^{\infty}(k+r-1)(f(x_k)-f^\star) \le \frac{(r-1)^2\|x_0-x^\star\|^2}{2s(r-3)}. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Low friction convergence under convexity of $(f-f^\star)^{(r-1)/2}$
assumptions: let $X$ be a solution to the ODE \eqref{eq:ode_r}
nodes.statement: Suppose $1 < r < 3$ and let $X$ be a solution to the ODE \eqref{eq:ode_r}. If $(f - f^\star)^{\frac{r-1}{2}}$ is also convex, then \begin{equation} f(X(t)) - f^\star \le \frac{(r-1)^2\|x_0 - x^\star\|^2}{2t^2}. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Convergence rate for strongly convex $f$ (continuous)
conclusions: the constant $C$ only depends on $\alpha$ and $r$
nodes.statement: For any $f\in\mathcal{S}_{\mu,L}(\R^n)$, if $2 \le \alpha \le 2r/3$ we get \begin{equation} f(X(t)) - f^\star \le \frac{C\|x_0-x^\star\|^2}{\mu^{\frac{\alpha-2}{2}}t^{\alpha}} \end{equation} for any $t > 0$. Above, the constant $C$ only depends on $\alpha$ and $r$.

nodes.name: Discrete $O(1/k^3)$ rate for strongly convex composite $f$
assumptions: Suppose $f$ is written as $f = g + h$, where $g\in\mathcal{S}_{\mu,L}$ and $h$ is convex with possible extended value $\infty$
the generalized Nesterov's scheme \eqref{eq:nesterov_general} with $r\geq 9/2$ and $s = 1/L$
nodes.statement: Suppose $f$ is written as $f = g + h$, where $g\in\mathcal{S}_{\mu,L}$ and $h$ is convex with possible extended value $\infty$. Then, the generalized Nesterov's scheme \eqref{eq:nesterov_general} with $r\geq 9/2$ and $s = 1/L$ satisfies \begin{equation} f(x_k) - f^\star \le \frac{CL\|x_0-x^\star\|^2}{k^2}\frac{\sqrt{L/\mu}}{k}, \end{equation} where $C$ only depends on $r$.

nodes.name: Linear convergence of speed restarting scheme
assumptions: There exist positive constants $c_1$ and $c_2$, which only depend on the condition number $L/\mu$
nodes.statement: There exist positive constants $c_1$ and $c_2$, which only depend on the condition number $L/\mu$, such that for any $f\in\mathcal{S}_{\mu, L}$, we have \begin{equation} f(\xsr(t)) - f^\star  \le \frac{c_1L\norm{x_0 - x^\star}^2}{2}\e{-c_2t\sqrt{L}}. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Convergence rate of the composite (nonsmooth) ODE
nodes.section: Appendix C. ODE for Composite Optimization
nodes.statement: Given a convex function $f(x)$ with directional subgradient $G(x, p;f)$, assume that the second order ODE \begin{equation} \ddot{X} + \frac{3}{t}\dot{X} + G(X, \dot X) = 0, ~ X(0) = x_0, \dot X(0) = 0 \end{equation} admits a solution $X(t)$ on $[0, \alpha)$ for some $\alpha > 0$. Then for any $0 < t < \alpha$, we have $$f(X(t)) - f^\star \le \frac{2\norm{x_0-x^\star}_2^2}{t^2}.$$

nodes.name: Nesterov's original convergence rate
nodes.statement: The original result from \citet{nesterov} states that, for any $f\in\mathcal{F}_L$, the sequence $\{x_k\}$ given by \eqref{eq:nesterov-scheme} with step size $s \le 1/L$ satisfies \begin{equation} f(x_k) - f^\star \le \frac{2\|x_0 - x^\star\|^2}{s(k+1)^2}. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Time Invariance
nodes.statement: If we adopt a linear time transformation, $\tilde t = ct$ for some $c > 0$, by the chain rule it follows that \begin{equation*} \frac{\d X}{\d \tilde t} = \frac{1}{c}\frac{\d X}{\d t}, ~ \frac{\d^2 X}{\d \tilde t^2} = \frac{1}{c^2}\frac{\d^2 X}{\d t^2}. \end{equation*} This yields the ODE parameterized by $\tilde t$, \begin{equation} \frac{\d^2 X}{\d \tilde t^2} + \frac{3}{\tilde t}\frac{\d X}{\d \tilde t} + \nabla f(X)/c^2 = 0. \end{equation} Also note that minimizing $f/c^2$ is equivalent to minimizing $f$. Hence, the ODE is invariant under the time change. In fact, it is easy to see that time invariance holds if and only if the coefficient of $\dot X$ has the form $C/t$ for some constant $C$.

nodes.name: Rotational Invariance
nodes.statement:
Nesterov's scheme and other gradient-based schemes are invariant under rotations. As expected, the ODE is also invariant under orthogonal transformation. To see this, let $Y = QX$ for some orthogonal matrix $Q$. This leads to $\dot Y = Q\dot X, \ddot Y = Q\ddot X$ and $
abla_Y f = Q
abla_X f$. Hence, denoting by $Q^T$ the transpose of $Q$, the ODE in the new coordinate system reads $Q^T\ddot Y +  rac{3}{t}Q^T\dot Y + Q^T
abla_Yf = 0$, which is of the same form as \eqref{key} once multiplying $Q$ on both sides.

nodes.name: Initial Asymptotic
nodes.statement:
Assume sufficient smoothness of $X$ such that $\lim_{t\goto 0} \ddot X(t)$ exists. The mean value theorem guarantees the existence of some $\xi\in(0, t)$ that satisfies $\dot X(t)/t = (\dot X(t) - \dot X(0))/t = \ddot X(\xi)$. Hence, from the ODE we deduce $\ddot X(t) + 3\dder{X}(\xi) + 
abla f(X(t)) = 0$. Taking the limit $t\goto 0$ gives $\ddot X(0) = -
abla f(x_0)/4$. Hence, for small $t$ we have the asymptotic form:  egin{equation} X(t) =  -  rac{
abla f(x_0)t^2}{8} + x_0 + o(t^2). \end{equation} This asymptotic expansion is consistent with the empirical observation that Nesterov's scheme moves slowly in the beginning.

nodes.name: Upper bound on $M(t)$
nodes.statement: For $t < \sqrt{12/L}$, we have \begin{equation} M(t) \le \frac{\norm{\nabla f(x_0)}}{4(1 - Lt^2/12)}. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Objective decays by a constant per restart
nodes.statement: There is a universal constant $C > 0$ such that \begin{equation} f(X(T)) - f^\star \le \left( 1 - \frac{C\mu}{L} \right) (f(x_0) - f^\star). \end{equation}

nodes.name: Upper bound on speed restarting time $T$
nodes.statement: There is a universal constant $\tilde C$ such that \[ T \le \frac{4\exp\left(\tilde C L/\mu\right)}{5\sqrt{L}}. \]

nodes.name: Existence of a solution to the ODE
nodes.statement: For any $f\in\mathcal{F}_{\infty}$ and any $x_0\in\R^n$, the ODE \eqref{key} has at least one solution $X$ in $C^{2}(0,\infty)\cap C^{1}[0,\infty)$.

nodes.name: Bound on $M_{\delta}(\delta)$
nodes.statement: For $\delta < \sqrt{6/L}$, we have \begin{equation} M_{\delta}(\delta) \le \frac{\norm{\nabla f(x_0)}}{1 - L\delta^2/6}. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Lipschitz gradient bound for the smoothed ODE
Bound on $M_{\delta}(t)$ for $t>\delta$
nodes.statement: For $\delta < \sqrt{6/L}$ and $\delta < t < \sqrt{12/L}$, we have \begin{equation} M_{\delta}(t) \le \frac{(5-L\delta^2/6)\norm{\nabla f(x_0)}}{4(1-L\delta^2/6)(1-Lt^2/12)}. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Uniform boundedness and equicontinuity of $\mathcal{F}$
nodes.statement: The function class $\mathcal{F} = \{X_{\delta}: \left[ 0, \sqrt{6/L}\right] \rightarrow \R^n \big{|} \delta = \sqrt{3/L}/2^m, m = 0, 1, \ldots\}$ is uniformly bounded and equicontinuous.

nodes.name: Uniqueness of the local solution
nodes.statement: For any $f \in \mathcal{F}_{\infty}$, the ODE \eqref{key} has at most one local solution in a neighborhood of $t=0$.

nodes.name: Gradient difference bound for two solutions
Euler scheme approximates Nesterov's scheme
nodes.statement: With step size $\Delta t = \sqrt{s}$, for any $T > 0$ we have \[ \max_{1 \le k \le \frac{T}{\sqrt{s}}}\|X_k^{\delta} - x_k\| \le C\delta^2 + o_s(1) \] for some constant $C$.

nodes.name: Directional derivative of a convex function
nodes.section: Appendix C. ODE for Composite Optimization
nodes.statement: For any convex function $f$ and any $x, p \in \R^n$, the directional derivative $\lim_{t\rightarrow 0+}(f(x + sp) - f(x))/s $ exists, and can be evaluated as $$\lim_{s\rightarrow 0+}\frac{f(x + sp) - f(x)}{s} = \sup_{\xi\in \partial f(x)}\langle \xi, p \rangle.$$

nodes.name: Lower bound on speed restarting time
nodes.section: Appendix E. Proof of Lemmas in Section \ref{sec:accelerate}
nodes.statement: The speed restarting time $T$ satisfies \[T(x_0, f) \geq \frac{4}{5\sqrt{L}}.\]

nodes.name: Speed Restarting Nesterov's Scheme
input: $x_0\in\R^n, y_0 = x_0, x_{-1} = x_0, 0 < s \le 1/L, k_{\max}\in\mathbb{N}^+$ and $k_{\min}\in\mathbb{N}^+$
nodes.statement: \begin{algorithmic} \STATE \textbf{input:} $x_0\in\R^n, y_0 = x_0, x_{-1} = x_0, 0 < s \le 1/L, k_{\max}\in\mathbb{N}^+$ and $k_{\min}\in\mathbb{N}^+$ \STATE $j \gets 1$ \FOR{$k = 1$ to $k_{\max}$} \STATE $x_k \gets \mbox{argmin}_x(\frac{1}{2s}\|x - y_{k-1} + s\nabla g(y_{k-1})\|^2 + h(x))$ \STATE $y_k \gets x_k + \frac{j-1}{j+2}(x_k - x_{k-1})$ \IF{ $\|x_k - x_{k-1}\| < \|x_{k-1} - x_{k-2}\|$ {\bf{and}} $j \ge k_{\min}$} \STATE $j \gets 1$ \ELSE \STATE $j \gets j + 1$ \ENDIF \ENDFOR \end{algorithmic}

nodes.name: Provable linear convergence for gradient restarting
nodes.statement: This leaves us an open problem of whether there exists provable linear convergence rate for the gradient restarting scheme as in Theorem \ref{exp}.

nodes.name: Conjectured tight bound $T = O(\sqrt{L}/\mu)$
nodes.statement: In closing, we remark that we believe that estimate in Lemma \ref{lm:decayfast} is tight, while not for Lemma \ref{lm:small}. Thus we conjecture that for a large class of $f\in\mathcal{S}_{\mu,L}$, if not all, $T = O(\sqrt{L}/\mu)$. If this is true, the exponent constant $c_2$ in Theorem \ref{exp} can be significantly improved.

nodes.name: Proof of inverse quadratic rate of the ODE
nodes.statement:
Consider the energy functional ootnote{We may also view this functional as the negative entropy. Similarly, for the gradient flow $\dot X + 
abla f(X) = 0$, an energy function of form $\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{gradient}}(t) = t(f(X(t))-f^\star) + \|X(t) - x^\star\|^2/2$ can be used to derive the bound $f(X(t)) - f^\star \le  rac{\|x_0-x^\star\|^2}{2t}$.} defined as $\mathcal{E}(t) = t^2(f(X(t)) - f^\star) + 2\|X + t\dot{X}/2 - x^\star \|^2$, whose time derivative is \[ \dot{\mathcal{E}} = 2t(f(X) - f^\star) + t^2\langle 
abla f, \dot{X} angle + 4\left\langle X +  rac{t}{2}\dot{X} - x^\star,  rac{3}{2}\dot{X} +  rac{t}{2}\ddot{X} ightangle. \] Substituting $3\dot{X}/2 + t\ddot{X}/2$ with $-t
abla f(X)/2$, the above equation gives \[ \dot{\mathcal{E}} = 2t(f(X) - f^\star) + 4\langle X - x^\star, - t
abla f(X)/2 angle  = 2t(f(X) - f^\star) -2t\langle X - x^\star, 
abla f(X) angle \le 0, \] where the inequality follows from the convexity of $f$. Hence by monotonicity of $\mathcal{E}$ and non-negativity of $2
orm{X + t\dot{X}/2 - x^\star}^2$, the gap satisfies  egin{equation*} f(X(t)) - f^\star \le  rac{\mathcal{E}(t)}{t^2} \le  rac{\mathcal{E}(0)}{t^2} =  rac{2
orm{x_0 - x^\star}^2}{t^2}. \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Proof of high friction convergence rate
nodes.statement:
Noting $r\dot{X} + t\ddot{X} = -t
abla f(X)$, we get $\dot{\mathcal{E}}$ equal to  egin{multline}  rac{4t}{r-1}(f(X) - f^\star) +  rac{2t^2}{r-1}\langle 
abla f, \dot{X} angle + 2\langle X +  rac{t}{r-1}\dot{X} - x^\star, r\dot{X} + t\ddot{X} angle\ =  rac{4t}{r-1}(f(X) - f^\star) - 2t\langle X - x^\star, 
abla f(X) angle \le - rac{2(r-3)t}{r-1}(f(X) - f^\star), \end{multline} where the inequality follows from the convexity of $f$. Since $f(X)\geq f^\star$, the last display implies that $\mathcal{E}$ is non-increasing. Hence  egin{equation}  rac{2t^2}{r-1}(f(X(t)) - f^\star) \le \mathcal{E}(t) \le \mathcal{E}(0) = (r-1)\|x_0 - x^\star\|^2, \end{equation} yielding the first inequality of this theorem. To complete the proof, from \eqref{eq:r_e_der} it follows that  egin{equation} \int^{\infty}_0 rac{2(r-3)t}{r-1}(f(X) - f^\star)\d t \le -\int^{\infty}_0  rac{\d\mathcal{E}}{\d t}\d t = \mathcal{E}(0) - \mathcal{E}(\infty) \le  (r-1)\|x_0 - x^\star\|^2, \end{equation} as desired for establishing the second inequality.

nodes.name: Proof of discrete high friction rate
nodes.statement: Consider the discrete energy functional, \begin{equation} \mathcal{E}(k) = \frac{2(k+r-2)^2s}{r-1}(f(x_k)-f^\star) + (r-1)\|z_k - x^\star\|^2, \end{equation} where $z_k = (k+r-1)y_k/(r-1) - kx_k/(r-1)$. If we have \begin{equation} \mathcal{E}(k) + \frac{2s[(r-3)(k+r-2)+1]}{r-1}(f(x_{k-1})-f^\star) \le \mathcal{E}(k-1), \end{equation} then it would immediately yield the desired results by summing \eqref{eq:recursive} over $k$. That is, by recursively applying \eqref{eq:recursive}, we see \begin{multline} \mathcal{E}(k) + \sum_{i=1}^k\frac{2s[(r-3)(i+r-2)+1]}{r-1}(f(x_{i-1})-f^\star) \\ \le \mathcal{E}(0) = \frac{2(r-2)^2s}{r-1}(f(x_0)-f^\star) + (r-1)\|x_0 - x^\star\|^2, \end{multline} which is equivalent to \begin{equation} \mathcal{E}(k) + \sum_{i=1}^{k-1}\frac{2s[(r-3)(i+r-1)+1]}{r-1}(f(x_{i})-f^\star) \le (r-1)\|x_0 - x^\star\|^2. \end{equation} Noting that the left-hand side of \eqref{eq:energy_bound} is lower bounded by $2s(k+r-2)^2(f(x_k)-f^\star)/(r-1)$, we thus obtain the first inequality of the theorem. Since $\mathcal{E}(k)\geq 0$, the second inequality is verified via taking the limit $k\goto\infty$ in \eqref{eq:energy_bound} and replacing $(r-3)(i+r-1)+1$ by $(r-3)(i+r-1)$. We now establish \eqref{eq:recursive}. For $s\le 1/L$, we have the basic inequality, \begin{equation} f(y-sG_s(y)) \le f(x) + G_s(y)^T(y-x) - \frac{s}{2}\|G_s(y)\|^2, \end{equation} for any $x$ and $y$. Note that $y_{k-1}-sG_s(y_{k-1})$ actually coincides with $x_k$. Summing of $(k-1)/(k+r-2)\times\eqref{eq:prox_ineq}$ with $x=x_{k-1}, y = y_{k-1}$ and $(r-1)/(k+r-2)\times\eqref{eq:prox_ineq}$ with $x=x^\star, y=y_{k-1}$ gives \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} f(x_k) &\le \frac{k-1}{k+r-2}f(x_{k-1}) + \frac{r-1}{k+r-2}f^\star\\ & + \frac{r-1}{k+r-2}G_s(y_{k-1})^T\Big{(}\frac{k+r-2}{r-1}y_{k-1}-\frac{k-1}{r-1}x_{k-1} - x^\star\Big{)} - \frac{s}{2}\|G_s(y_{k-1})\|^2\\ &= \frac{k-1}{k+r-2}f(x_{k-1}) + \frac{r-1}{k+r-2}f^\star + \frac{(r-1)^2}{2s(k+r-2)^2}\Big{(}\|z_{k-1}-x^\star\|^2 - \|z_{k}-x^\star\|^2\Big{)}, \\ \end{aligned} \end{equation} where we use $z_{k-1}-s(k+r-2)G_s(y_{k-1})/(r-1)=z_{k}$. Rearranging the above inequality and multiplying by $2s(k+r-2)^2/(r-1)$ gives the desired \eqref{eq:recursive}.

nodes.name: Proof of low friction convergence
nodes.statement:
Since $(f - f^\star)^{ rac{r-1}{2}}$ is convex, we obtain \[ \left( f(X(t)) - f^\star ight)^{ rac{r-1}{2}} \le \langle X - x^\star, 
abla(f(X) - f^\star)^{ rac{r-1}{2}} angle =  rac{r-1}{2}(f(X) - f^\star)^{ rac{r-3}{2}}\langle X - x^\star, 
abla f(X)angle, \] which can be simplified to $ rac{2}{r-1}(f(X) - f^\star) \le \langle X - x^\star, 
abla f(X)angle$. This inequality combined with \eqref{eq:r_e_der} leads to the monotonically decreasing of $\mathcal{E}(t)$ defined for Theorem ef{thm:large_r}. This completes the proof by noting $f(X)-f^\star\le (r-1)\mathcal{E}(t)/(2t^2)\le (r-1)\mathcal{E}(0)/(2t^2) = (r-1)^2\|x_0 - x^\star\|^2/(2t^2)$.

nodes.name: Proof of strongly convex continuous rate (induction on $lpha$)
nodes.statement: Note that $\dot{\mathcal{E}}(t; \alpha)$ equals \begin{multline} \alpha t^{\alpha - 1}(f(X)-f^\star) - \frac{(2r-\alpha)t^{\alpha-1}}{2}\langle X- x^\star, \nabla f(X)\rangle + \frac{(\alpha-2)(2r-\alpha)^2t^{\alpha-3}}{8}\|X-x^\star\|^2 \\+ \frac{(\alpha-2)(2r-\alpha)t^{\alpha-2}}{4}\langle \dot X, X - x^\star\rangle. \end{multline} By the strong convexity of $f$, the second term of the right-hand side of \eqref{eq:alpha_energy} is bounded below as \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \frac{(2r-\alpha)t^{\alpha-1}}{2}\langle X- x^\star, \nabla f(X)\rangle \geq \frac{(2r-\alpha)t^{\alpha-1}}{2}(f(X) -f^\star) + \frac{\mu(2r-\alpha)t^{\alpha-1}}{4}\|X-x^\star\|^2. \end{aligned} \end{equation} Substituting the last display  into \eqref{eq:alpha_energy} with the awareness of $r \geq 3\alpha/2$ yields \begin{multline} \dot{\mathcal{E}} \le -  \frac{(2\mu(2r-\alpha)t^2 - (\alpha-2)(2r-\alpha)^2)t^{\alpha-3}}{8}\|X-x^\star\|^2 + \frac{(\alpha-2)(2r-\alpha)t^{\alpha-2}}{8}\frac{\d\|X-x^\star\|^2}{\d t}. \end{multline} Hence, if $t \geq t_{\alpha} :=  \sqrt{(\alpha-2)(2r-\alpha)/(2\mu)}$, we obtain \begin{equation} \dot{\mathcal{E}}(t) \le \frac{(\alpha-2)(2r-\alpha)t^{\alpha-2}}{8}\frac{\d\|X-x^\star\|^2}{\d t}. \end{equation} Integrating the last inequality on the interval $(t_{\alpha}, t)$ gives \begin{multline} \mathcal{E}(t) \le \mathcal{E}(t_{\alpha}) + \frac{(\alpha-2)(2r-\alpha)t^{\alpha-2}}{8}\|X(t)-x^\star\|^2 - \frac{(\alpha-2)(2r-\alpha)t_{\alpha}^{\alpha-2}}{8}\|X(t_{\alpha})-x^\star\|^2 \\- \inverse{8}\int^t_{t_{\alpha}}(\alpha-2)^2(2r-\alpha)u^{\alpha-3}\|X(u)-x^\star\|^2\d u \le \mathcal{E}(t_{\alpha}) + \frac{(\alpha-2)(2r-\alpha)t^{\alpha-2}}{8}\|X(t)-x^\star\|^2\\ \le \mathcal{E}(t_{\alpha}) + \frac{(\alpha-2)(2r-\alpha)t^{\alpha-2}}{4\mu}(f(X(t)) - f^\star). \end{multline} Making use of \eqref{eq:bound_tilde_energy}, we apply induction on $\alpha$ to finish the proof. First, consider $2 < \alpha \le 4$. Applying Theorem \ref{thm:large_r}, from \eqref{eq:bound_tilde_energy} we get that $\mathcal{E}(t)$ is upper bounded by \begin{equation} \mathcal{E}(t_{\alpha}) + \frac{(\alpha-2)(r-1)^2(2r-\alpha)\|x_0-x^\star\|^2}{8\mu t^{4-\alpha}} \le \mathcal{E}(t_{\alpha}) + \frac{(\alpha-2)(r-1)^2(2r-\alpha)\|x_0-x^\star\|^2}{8\mu t_{\alpha}^{4-\alpha}}. \end{equation} Then, we bound $\mathcal{E}(t_{\alpha})$ as follows. \begin{multline} \mathcal{E}(t_{\alpha}) \le t_{\alpha}^{\alpha}(f(X(t_{\alpha})) - f^\star) + \frac{(2r-\alpha)^2t_{\alpha}^{\alpha-2}}{4}\Big{\|}\frac{2r-2}{2r-\alpha}X(t_{\alpha})+ \frac{2t_{\alpha}}{2r-\alpha}\dot X(t_{\alpha}) - \frac{2r-2}{2r-\alpha}x^\star\Big{\|}^2\\ + \frac{(2r-\alpha)^2t_{\alpha}^{\alpha-2}}{4}\Big{\|}\frac{\alpha-2}{2r-\alpha}X(t_{\alpha})  - \frac{\alpha-2}{2r-\alpha}x^\star\Big{\|}^2 \\ \le (r-1)^2t_{\alpha}^{\alpha-2}\|x_0-x^\star\|^2 + \frac{(\alpha-2)^2(r-1)^2\|x_0-x^\star\|^2}{4\mu t_{\alpha}^{4-\alpha}}, \end{multline} where in the second inequality we use the decreasing property of the energy functional defined for Theorem \ref{thm:large_r}. Combining \eqref{eq:simple_bound_tilde_energy} and \eqref{eq:general_alpha_bound}, we have \begin{equation} \mathcal{E}(t) \le (r-1)^2t_{\alpha}^{\alpha-2}\|x_0-x^\star\|^2 + \frac{(\alpha-2)(r-1)^2(2r+\alpha-4)\|x_0-x^\star\|^2}{8\mu t_{\alpha}^{4-\alpha}} = O \Big{(} \frac{\|x_0-x^\star\|^2}{\mu^{\frac{\alpha-2}{2}}}  \Big{)}. \end{equation} For $t \ge t_{\alpha}$, it suffices to apply $f(X(t))-f^\star\le \mathcal{E}(t)/t^3$ to the last display. For $t < t_{\alpha}$, by Theorem \ref{thm:large_r}, $f(X(t)) - f^\star$ is upper bounded by \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \frac{(r-1)^2\|x_0 - x^\star\|^2}{2t^2} &\le \frac{(r-1)^2\mu^{\frac{\alpha-2}{2}}[(\alpha-2)(2r-\alpha)/(2\mu)]^{\frac{\alpha-2}{2}}}{2}\frac{\|x_0-x^\star\|^2}{\mu^{\frac{\alpha-2}{2}}t^{\alpha}} \\ &= O\Big{(}\frac{\|x_0-x^\star\|^2}{\mu^{\frac{\alpha-2}{2}}t^{\alpha}} \Big{)}. \end{aligned} \end{equation} Next, suppose that the theorem is valid for some $\tilde{\alpha} > 2$. We show below that this theorem is still valid for $\alpha := \tilde{\alpha} + 1$ if still $r \geq 3\alpha/2$. By the assumption, \eqref{eq:bound_tilde_energy} further induces \begin{equation} \mathcal{E}(t) \le \mathcal{E}(t_{\alpha}) + \frac{(\alpha-2)(2r-\alpha)t^{\alpha-2}}{4\mu}\frac{\tilde{C}\|x_0 - x^\star\|^2}{\mu^{\frac{\tilde{\alpha}-2}{2}}t^{\tilde{\alpha}}} \le \mathcal{E}(t_{\alpha}) + \frac{\tilde{C}(\alpha-2)(2r-\alpha)\|x_0 - x^\star\|^2}{4\mu^{\frac{\alpha-1}{2}}t_{\alpha}} \end{equation} for some constant $\tilde C$ only depending on $\tilde{\alpha}$ and $r$. This inequality with \eqref{eq:general_alpha_bound} implies \begin{align*} \mathcal{E}(t)  &\le (r-1)^2t_{\alpha}^{\alpha-2}\|x_0-x^\star\|^2 + \frac{(\alpha-2)^2(r-1)^2\|x_0-x^\star\|^2}{4\mu t_{\alpha}^{4-\alpha}} + \frac{\tilde{C}(\alpha-2)(2r-\alpha)\|x_0 - x^\star\|^2}{4\mu^{\frac{\alpha-1}{2}}t_{\alpha}} \\ &= O\left( \|x_0-x^\star\|^2/\mu^{\frac{\alpha-2}{2}} \right), \end{align*} which verify the induction for $t \geq t_{\alpha}$. As for $t < t_{\alpha}$, the validity of the induction follows from Theorem \ref{thm:large_r}, similarly to \eqref{eq:alpha_general_alpha_small_t}. Thus, combining the base and induction steps, the proof is completed.

nodes.name: Proof of linear convergence of speed restarting
nodes.statement: Note that Lemma \ref{lm:small} asserts, by time $t$ at least $m := \lfloor 5t\sqrt{L}\e{-\tilde C L/\mu}/4\rfloor$ restartings have occurred for $\xsr$. Hence, recursively applying Lemma \ref{lm:decayfast}, we have \begin{align*} f(\xsr(t)) - f^\star &\le f \left( \xsr(T_1 + \cdots + T_m) \right) - f^\star \\ &\le (1 - C\mu/L) \left(f \left( \xsr(T_1 + \cdots + T_{m-1}) \right) - f^\star \right)\\ & \le \cdots \le \cdots \\ &\le (1 - C\mu/L)^m (f(x_0) - f^\star)  \le \e{- C\mu m/L} (f(x_0) - f^\star) \\ &\le c_1\e{-c_2t\sqrt{L}}(f(x_0) - f^\star) \le \frac{c_1L\|x_0 - x^\star\|^2}{2}\e{-c_2t\sqrt{L}}, \end{align*} where $c_1 = \exp(C\mu/L)$ and $c_2 = 5C\mu e^{-\tilde C \mu/L}/(4L)$.

It suffices to establish that $\mathcal{E}$, first defined in the proof of Theorem ef{thm:ode_rate}, is monotonically decreasing. The difficulty comes from that $\mathcal E$ may not be differentiable in this setting. Instead, we study $(\mathcal{E}(t + \D t) - \mathcal{E}(t))/\D t$ for small $\D t > 0$. In $\mathcal{E}$, the second term $2
orm{X + t\dot{X}/2 - x^\star}^2$ is differentiable, with derivative $4\langle X +  rac{t}{2}\dot X- x^\star,  rac{3}{2}\dot X +  rac{t}{2}\ddot X angle$. Hence,  egin{equation}  egin{aligned} & 2
orm{X(t + \D t) +  rac{t}{2}\dot{X}(t + \D t) - x^\star}^2 - 2
orm{X(t) +  rac{t}{2}\dot{X}(t) - x^\star}^2\ & = 4\langle X +  rac{t}{2}\dot X- x^\star,  rac{3}{2}\dot X +  rac{t}{2}\ddot X angle\D t + o(\D t)\ & = -t^2\langle \dot X, G(X, \dot X)angle\D t - 2t\langle X -x^\star, G(X, \dot X)angle\D t+ o(\D t). \end{aligned} \end{equation} For the first term, note that  egin{multline} (t + \D t)^2(f(X(t + \D t)) -f^\star) - t^2(f(X(t)) -f^\star) = 2t(f(X(t+\D t)) - f^\star)\D t + \ t^2 (f(X(t + \D t)) - f(X(t)))+ o(\D t). \end{multline} Since $f$ is locally Lipschitz, $o(\D t)$ term does not affect the function in the limit,  egin{equation} f(X(t+\D t)) = f(X + \D t \dot X + o(\D t)) = f(X + \D t \dot X) + o(\D t). \end{equation} By Lemma ef{rock}, we have the approximation  egin{equation} f(X + \D t \dot X) = f(X) +  \langle \dot X,G(X, \dot X)angle\D t + o(\D t). \end{equation} Combining all of \eqref{eq:energy_diff_first}, \eqref{eq:local_lip} and \eqref{eq:approx_grow}, we obtain  egin{gather*} \mathcal{E}(t + \D t) - \mathcal{E}(t) = 2t(f(X(t+\D t)) - f^\star)\D t + t^2\langle\dot X,G(X,\dot X) angle\D t -t^2\langle \dot X, G(X, \dot X)angle\D t \ - 2t\langle X -x^\star, G(X, \dot X)angle\D t+ o(\D t)\ =2t(f(X) - f^\star)\D t - 2t\langle X -x^\star, G(X, \dot X)angle\D t+ o(\D t)\le o(\D t), \end{gather*} where the last inequality follows from the convexity of $f$. Thus, $$\limsup_{\D tightarrow 0+} rac{\mathcal{E}(t+\D t)-\mathcal{E}(t)}{\D t} \le 0,$$ which along with the continuity of $\mathcal{E}$, concludes that $\mathcal{E}(t)$ is a non-increasing function of $t$.

Let $z_k = (x_{k+1} - x_k)/\sqrt{s}$. Then Nesterov's scheme is equivalent to  egin{equation}  egin{aligned} x_{k+1} &= x_k + \sqrt{s}z_k\ z_{k+1} & = \Big( 1 -  rac3{k+3} \Big) z_k - \sqrt{s}

abla f(x_0)\|\sqrt{s}$. The idea of this proof is to bound $a_k$ via simultaneously estimating $a_k$ and $b_k$. By comparing \eqref{eq:euler_x_z} and \eqref{eq:nesterov_x_z}, we get the iterative relationship for $a_k$: $a_{k+1} \le a_k + \sqrt{s}b_k$. Denoting by $S_k = b_0 + b_1 + \cdots + b_k$, this yields  egin{equation} a_k \le \sqrt{s}S_{k-1}. \end{equation} Similarly, for sufficiently small $s$ we get \[  egin{aligned} b_{k+1} &\le \Big| 1 -  rac{3}{\max\{\delta/\sqrt{s}, k \}} \Big| b_k + L\sqrt{s}a_k + \Big(\Big| rac3{k+3} -  rac3{\max\{\delta/\sqrt{s}, k\}} \Big| + 2Ls  \Big)\|z_k\|\ & \le b_k + L\sqrt{s}a_k + \Big(\Big| rac3{k+3} -  rac3{\max\{\delta/\sqrt{s}, k\}} \Big| + 2Ls  \Big)\|z_k\|. \end{aligned} \] To upper bound $\|z_k\|$, denoting by $C_1$ the supremum of $\sqrt{2L(f(y_k) - f^\star)}$ over all $k$ and $s$, we have \[ \|z_k\| \le  rac{k - 1}{k + 2}\|z_{k-1}\|  + \sqrt{s}\|
abla f(y_k)\| \le \|z_{k-1}\|  + C_1\sqrt{s}, \] which gives $\|z_k\| \le C_1(k + 1)\sqrt{s}$. Hence,  egin{equation} \Big(\Big| rac3{k+3} -  rac3{\max\{\delta/\sqrt{s}, k\}} \Big| + 2Ls \Big)\|z_k\| \le  egin{cases} C_2\sqrt{s}, \quad k \le  rac{\delta}{\sqrt{s}}\  rac{C_2\sqrt{s}}{k} <  rac{C_2s}{\delta}, \quad k >  rac{\delta}{\sqrt{s}}.\ \end{cases} \end{equation} Making use of \eqref{eq:diff_x_z} gives  egin{equation} b_{k +1} \le  egin{cases} b_k + LsS_{k-1} + C_2\sqrt{s}, \quad k \le \delta/\sqrt{s}\ b_k + LsS_{k-1} +  rac{C_2s}{\delta}, \quad k > \delta/\sqrt{s}.\ \end{cases} \end{equation} By induction on $k$, for $k \le \delta/\sqrt{s}$ it holds that \[ b_k \le  rac{C_1Ls + C_2 + (C_1+C_2)\sqrt{Ls}}{2\sqrt{L}}(1 + \sqrt{Ls})^{k-1} -  rac{C_1Ls + C_2 - (C_1+C_2)\sqrt{Ls}}{2\sqrt{L}}(1 - \sqrt{Ls})^{k-1}. \] Hence, \[ S_k \le  rac{C_1Ls + C_2 + (C_1+C_2)\sqrt{Ls}}{2L\sqrt{s}}(1 + \sqrt{Ls})^{k} +  rac{C_1Ls + C_2 - (C_1+C_2)\sqrt{Ls}}{2L\sqrt{s}}(1 - \sqrt{Ls})^k -  rac{C_2}{L\sqrt{s}}. \] Letting $k^\star = \lfloor \delta/\sqrt{s} floor$, we get \[ \limsup_{s \goto 0} \sqrt{s}S_{k^\star-1} \le  rac{C_2\e{\delta\sqrt{L}} + C_2 \e{-\delta\sqrt{L}} - 2C_2}{2L} = O(\delta^2), \] which allows us to conclude that  egin{equation} a_k \le \sqrt{s}S_{k-1} = O(\delta^2) + o_s(1) \end{equation} for all $k \le \delta/\sqrt{s}$. Next, we bound $b_k$ for $k > k^\star = \lfloor \delta/\sqrt{s} floor$. To this end, we consider the worst case of \eqref{eq:bk_iterative}, that is, \[ b_{k+1} = b_k + LsS_{k-1} +  rac{C_2s}{\delta} \] for $k > k^\star$ and $S_{k^\star} = S_{k^\star+1} = C_3\delta^2/\sqrt{s} + o_s(1/\sqrt{s})$ for some sufficiently large $C_3$. In this case, $C_2s/\delta < sS_{k-1}$ for sufficiently small $s$. Hence, the last display gives \[ b_{k+1} \le b_k + (L+1)sS_{k-1}. \] By induction, we get \[ S_k \le  rac{C_3\delta^2/\sqrt{s} + o_s(1/\sqrt{s})}{2}\left( (1+\sqrt{(L+1)s})^{k-k^\star} +  (1-\sqrt{(L+1)s})^{k-k^\star} ight). \] Letting $k^\diamond = \lfloor T/\sqrt{s} floor$, we further get \[ \limsup_{s\goto 0} \sqrt{s}S_{k^\diamond} \le  rac{C_3\delta^2(\e{(T-\delta)\sqrt{L+1}} + \e{-(T-\delta)\sqrt{L+1}})}{2} = O(\delta^2), \] which yields  egin{equation} a_k \le \sqrt{s}S_{k-1} = O(\delta^2) + o_s(1) \end{equation} for $k^\star < k \le k^\diamond$. Last, combining \eqref{eq:ak_bound_delta} and the last display, we get the desired result.

nodes.name: Proof of discrete $O(1/k^3)$ rate (Theorem dis_t3)
nodes.statement: Let $g$ be $\mu$--strongly convex and $h$ be convex. For $f = g + h$, we show that \eqref{eq:prox_ineq} can be strengthened to \begin{equation} f(y-sG_s(y)) \le f(x) + G_s(y)^T(y-x) - \frac{s}{2}\|G_s(y)\|^2 - \frac{\mu}{2}\|y-x\|^2. \end{equation} Summing $(4k-3)\times\eqref{eq:str_prox}$ with $x = x_{k-1}, y=y_{k-1}$ and $(4r-6)\times\eqref{eq:str_prox}$ with $x = x^\star, y=y_{k-1}$ yields \begin{multline} (4k+4r-9)f(x_k)\le (4k-3)f(x_{k-1}) + (4r-6)f^\star \\ + G_s(y_{k-1})^T[(4k+4r-9)y_{k-1} - (4k-3)x_{k-1}-(4r-6)x^\star]\\ - \frac{s(4k+4r-9)}{2}\|G_s(y_{k-1})\|^2 - \frac{\mu(4k-3)}{2}\|y_{k-1}-x_{k-1}\|^2 - \mu(2r-3)\|y_{k-1}-x^\star\|^2\\ \le (4k-3)f(x_{k-1}) + (4r-6)f^\star - \mu(2r-3)\|y_{k-1}-x^\star\|^2\\ + G_s(y_{k-1})^T\left[ (4k+4r-9)(y_{k-1}-x^\star) - (4k-3)(x_{k-1}-x^\star) \right], \end{multline} which gives a lower bound on $G_s(y_{k-1})^T \left[ (4k+4r-9)y_{k-1} - (4k-3)x_{k-1}-(4r-6)x^\star \right]$. Denote by $\Delta_k$ the second term of $\tilde{\mathcal{E}}(k)$ in \eqref{eq:dis_t3_energy}, namely, \[ \Delta_k \triangleq \frac{k+d}{8}\|(2k+2r-2)(y_k-x^\star) - (2k+1)(x_k-x^\star)\|^2, \] where $d := 3r/2-5/2$. Then by \eqref{eq:bound_for_g}, we get \begin{multline} \Delta_k - \Delta_{k-1} = -\frac{k+d}{8}\Big\langle s(2r+2k-5)G_s(y_{k-1})+\frac{k-2}{k+r-2}(x_{k-1}-x_{k-2}), (4k+4r-9)(y_{k-1}-x^\star) \\ - (4k-3)(x_{k-1}-x^\star) \Big\rangle + \frac{1}{8}\|(2k+2r-4)(y_{k-1}-x^\star) - (2k-1)(x_{k-1}-x^\star)\|^2\\ \le -\frac{s(k+d)(2k+2r-5)}{8} \big[(4k+4r-9)(f(x_k)-f^\star)\\ -(4k-3)(f(x_{k-1})-f^\star) + \mu(2r-3)\|y_{k-1}-x^\star\|^2 \big]\\ -\frac{(k+d)(k-2)}{8(k+r-2)}\left\langle x_{k-1}-x_{k-2}, (4k+4r-9)(y_{k-1}-x^\star)-(4k-3)(x_{k-1}-x^\star) \right\rangle \\+ \frac{1}{8}\|2(k+r-2)(y_{k-1}-x^\star) - (2k-1)(x_{k-1}-x^\star)\|^2.\\ \end{multline} Hence, \begin{multline} \Delta_k + \frac{s(k+d)(2k+2r-5)(4k+4r-9)}{8}(f(x_k)-f^\star)\\ \le \Delta_{k-1} + \frac{s(k+d)(2k+2r-5)(4k-3)}{8}(f(x_{k-1})-f^\star)\\ -\frac{s\mu(2r-3)(k+d)(2k+2r-5)}{8}\|y_{k-1}-x^\star\|^2 + \Pi_1 + \Pi_2, \end{multline} where \begin{equation} \Pi_1 \triangleq -\frac{(k+d)(k-2)}{8(k+r-2)}\langle x_{k-1}-x_{k-2}, (4k+4r-9)(y_{k-1}-x^\star)-(4k-3)(x_{k-1}-x^\star)\rangle, \end{equation} \begin{equation} \Pi_2 \triangleq \frac{1}{8}\|2(k+r-2)(y_{k-1}-x^\star) - (2k-1)(x_{k-1}-x^\star)\|^2. \end{equation} By the iterations defined in \eqref{eq:nesterov_general}, one can show that \begin{multline} \Pi_1 = -\frac{(2r-3)(k+d)(k-2)}{8(k+r-2)}(\|x_{k-1} - x^\star\|^2 - \|x_{k-2} - x^\star\|^2) \\- \frac{(k-2)^2(4k+4r-9)(k+d) + (2r-3)(k-2)(k+r-2)(k+d)}{8(k+r-2)^2}\|x_{k-1}-x_{k-2}\|^2, \end{multline} \begin{multline} \Pi_2 = \frac{(2r-3)^2}{8}\|y_{k-1}-x^\star\|^2 + \frac{(2r-3)(2k-1)(k-2)}{8(k+r-2)}(\|x_{k-1} - x^\star\|^2 - \|x_{k-2} - x^\star\|^2) \\+ \frac{(k-2)^2(2k-1)(2k+4r-7) + (2r-3)(2k-1)(k-2)(k+r-2)}{8(k+r-2)^2}\|x_{k-1}-x_{k-2}\|^2. \end{multline} Although this is a little tedious, it is straightforward to check that $(k-2)^2(4k+4r-9)(k+d) + (2r-3)(k-2)(k+r-2)(k+d) \geq (k-2)^2(2k-1)(2k+4r-7) + (2r-3)(2k-1)(k-2)(k+r-2)$ for any $k$. Therefore, $\Pi_1 + \Pi_2$ is bounded as \begin{equation} \Pi_1 + \Pi_2 \le \frac{(2r-3)^2}{8}\|y_{k-1}-x^\star\|^2 + \frac{(2r-3)(k-d-1)(k-2)}{8(k+r-2)}(\|x_{k-1} - x^\star\|^2 - \|x_{k-2} - x^\star\|^2), \end{equation} which, together with the fact that $s\mu(2r-3)(k+d)(2k+2r-5) \geq (2r-3)^2$ when $k\geq \sqrt{(2r-3)/(2s\mu)}$, reduces \eqref{eq:prox_main_t3} to \begin{multline} \Delta_k + \frac{s(k+d)(2k+2r-5)(4k+4r-9)}{8}(f(x_k)-f^\star)\\ \le \Delta_{k-1} + \frac{s(k+d)(2k+2r-5)(4k-3)}{8}(f(x_{k-1})-f^\star) \\+ \frac{(2r-3)(k-d-1)(k-2)}{8(k+r-2)}(\|x_{k-1} - x^\star\|^2 - \|x_{k-2} - x^\star\|^2). \end{multline} This can be further simplified as \begin{equation} \tilde{\mathcal{E}}(k) + A_k(f(x_{k-1})-f^\star) \le \tilde{\mathcal{E}}(k-1) + B_k(\|x_{k-1} - x^\star\|^2 - \|x_{k-2} - x^\star\|^2) \end{equation} for $k\geq \sqrt{(2r-3)/(2s\mu)}$, where $A_k = (8r-36)k^2+(20r^2-126r+200)k+12r^3-100r^2+288r-281 > 0$ since $r\geq 9/2$ and $B_k = (2r-3)(k-d-1)(k-2)/(8(k+r-2))$. Denote by $k^\star = \lceil\max\{\sqrt{(2r-3)/(2s\mu)}, 3r/2-3/2\}\rceil \asymp 1/\sqrt{s\mu}$. Then $B_k$ is a positive increasing sequence if $k > k^\star$. Summing \eqref{eq:prox_main_t3_2} from $k$ to $k^\star + 1$, we obtain \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} &\mathcal{E}(k) + \sum_{i=k^\star+1}^k A_i(f(x_{i-1}) - f^\star) \le \mathcal{E}(k^\star) + \sum_{i=k^\star+1}^k B_i(\|x_{i-1} - x^\star\|^2 - \|x_{i-2} - x^\star\|^2)\\ & = \mathcal{E}(k^\star) + B_k\|x_{k-1} - x^\star\|^2 - B_{k^\star+1}\|x_{k^\star-1} - x^\star\|^2 + \sum_{i=k^\star+1}^{k-1} (B_{j} - B_{j+1})\|x_{j-1} - x^\star\|^2\\ &\le \mathcal{E}(k^\star) + B_k\|x_{k-1} - x^\star\|^2. \end{aligned} \end{equation} Similarly, as in the proof of Theorem \ref{thm:cube_rate}, we can bound $\mathcal{E}(k^\star)$ via another energy functional defined from Theorem \ref{thm:large_r}, \begin{multline} \mathcal{E}(k^\star) \le \frac{s(2k^\star+3r-5)(k^\star+r-2)^2}{2}(f(x_{k^\star}) - f^\star) \\+ \frac{2k^\star+3r-5}{16}\|2(k^\star+r-1)y_{k^\star} - 2k^\star x_{k^\star} - 2(r-1)x^\star -(x_{k^\star} - x^\star)\|^2\\ \le \frac{s(2k^\star+3r-5)(k^\star+r-2)^2}{2}(f(x_{k^\star}) - f^\star) \\ + \frac{2k^\star+3r-5}{8}\|2(k^\star+r-1)y_{k^\star} - 2k^\star x_{k^\star} - 2(r-1)x^\star\|^2\\ + \frac{2k^\star+3r-5}{8}\|x_{k^\star} - x^\star\|^2 \le \frac{(r-1)^2(2k^\star+3r-5)}{2}\|x_0 - x^\star\|^2 \\+ \frac{(r-1)^2(2k^\star+3r-5)}{8s\mu(k^\star+r-2)^2}\|x_0 - x^\star\|^2 \lesssim \frac{\|x_0-x^\star\|^2}{\sqrt{s\mu}}. \end{multline} For the second term, it follows from Theorem \ref{thm:large_r_dis} that \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} B_k\|x_{k-1} - x^\star\|^2 &\le  \frac{(2r-3)(2k-3r+3)(k-2)}{8\mu(k+r-2)}(f(x_{k-1}) - x^\star)\\ &\le \frac{(2r-3)(2k-3r+3)(k-2)}{8\mu(k+r-2)}\frac{(r-1)^2\|x_0-x^\star\|^2}{2s(k+r-3)^2} \\ &\le \frac{(2r-3)(r-1)^2(2k^\star-3r+3)(k^\star-2)}{16s\mu(k^\star+r-2)(k^\star+r-3)^2} \|x_0-x^\star\|^2 \lesssim  \frac{\|x_0-x^\star\|^2}{\sqrt{s\mu}}. \end{aligned} \end{equation} For $k > k^\star$, \eqref{eq:ener_dis_bound1} together with \eqref{eq:ener_dis_bound2} this gives \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} f(x_k)-f^\star &\le \frac{16\mathcal{E}(k)}{s(2k+3r-5)(2k+2r-5)(4k+4r-9)}\\ &\le \frac{16(\mathcal{E}(k^\star) + B_k\|x_{k-1}-x^\star\|^2)}{s(2k+3r-5)(2k+2r-5)(4k+4r-9)} \lesssim \frac{\|x_0 - x^\star\|^2}{s^{\frac{3}{2}}\mu^{\half}k^3}. \end{aligned} \end{equation} To conclusion, note that by Theorem \ref{thm:large_r_dis} the gap $f(x_k) - f^\star$ for $k \le k^\star$ is bounded by \begin{equation} \frac{(r-1)^2\|x_0-x^\star\|^2}{2s(k+r-2)^2} = \frac{(r-1)^2\sqrt{s\mu}k^3}{2(k+r-2)^2}\frac{\|x_0 - x^\star\|^2}{s^{\frac{3}{2}}\mu^{\half}k^3} \lesssim \sqrt{s\mu}k^\star\frac{\|x_0 - x^\star\|^2}{s^{\frac{3}{2}}\mu^{\half}k^3} \lesssim \frac{\|x_0 - x^\star\|^2}{s^{\frac{3}{2}}\mu^{\half}k^3}. \end{equation}

nodes.name: First inequality (energy monotonicity)
nodes.statement:
Noting $r\dot{X} + t\ddot{X} = -t
abla f(X)$, we get $\dot{\mathcal{E}}$ equal to  egin{multline}  rac{4t}{r-1}(f(X) - f^\star) +  rac{2t^2}{r-1}\langle 
abla f, \dot{X} angle + 2\langle X +  rac{t}{r-1}\dot{X} - x^\star, r\dot{X} + t\ddot{X} angle\ =  rac{4t}{r-1}(f(X) - f^\star) - 2t\langle X - x^\star, 
abla f(X) angle \le - rac{2(r-3)t}{r-1}(f(X) - f^\star), \end{multline} where the inequality follows from the convexity of $f$. Since $f(X)\geq f^\star$, the last display implies that $\mathcal{E}$ is non-increasing. Hence  egin{equation}  rac{2t^2}{r-1}(f(X(t)) - f^\star) \le \mathcal{E}(t) \le \mathcal{E}(0) = (r-1)\|x_0 - x^\star\|^2, \end{equation} yielding the first inequality of this theorem.

nodes.name: Second inequality (integrated bound)
nodes.statement: To complete the proof, from \eqref{eq:r_e_der} it follows that \begin{equation} \int^{\infty}_0\frac{2(r-3)t}{r-1}(f(X) - f^\star)\d t \le -\int^{\infty}_0 \frac{\d\mathcal{E}}{\d t}\d t = \mathcal{E}(0) - \mathcal{E}(\infty) \le  (r-1)\|x_0 - x^\star\|^2, \end{equation} as desired for establishing the second inequality.

nodes.name: Derive the theorem from the recursive inequality
nodes.statement: Consider the discrete energy functional, \begin{equation} \mathcal{E}(k) = \frac{2(k+r-2)^2s}{r-1}(f(x_k)-f^\star) + (r-1)\|z_k - x^\star\|^2, \end{equation} where $z_k = (k+r-1)y_k/(r-1) - kx_k/(r-1)$. If we have \begin{equation} \mathcal{E}(k) + \frac{2s[(r-3)(k+r-2)+1]}{r-1}(f(x_{k-1})-f^\star) \le \mathcal{E}(k-1), \end{equation} then it would immediately yield the desired results by summing \eqref{eq:recursive} over $k$. That is, by recursively applying \eqref{eq:recursive}, we see \begin{multline} \mathcal{E}(k) + \sum_{i=1}^k\frac{2s[(r-3)(i+r-2)+1]}{r-1}(f(x_{i-1})-f^\star) \\ \le \mathcal{E}(0) = \frac{2(r-2)^2s}{r-1}(f(x_0)-f^\star) + (r-1)\|x_0 - x^\star\|^2, \end{multline} which is equivalent to \begin{equation} \mathcal{E}(k) + \sum_{i=1}^{k-1}\frac{2s[(r-3)(i+r-1)+1]}{r-1}(f(x_{i})-f^\star) \le (r-1)\|x_0 - x^\star\|^2. \end{equation} Noting that the left-hand side of \eqref{eq:energy_bound} is lower bounded by $2s(k+r-2)^2(f(x_k)-f^\star)/(r-1)$, we thus obtain the first inequality of the theorem. Since $\mathcal{E}(k)\geq 0$, the second inequality is verified via taking the limit $k\goto\infty$ in \eqref{eq:energy_bound} and replacing $(r-3)(i+r-1)+1$ by $(r-3)(i+r-1)$.

nodes.name: Establish the recursive inequality
nodes.statement: We now establish \eqref{eq:recursive}. For $s\le 1/L$, we have the basic inequality, \begin{equation} f(y-sG_s(y)) \le f(x) + G_s(y)^T(y-x) - \frac{s}{2}\|G_s(y)\|^2, \end{equation} for any $x$ and $y$. Note that $y_{k-1}-sG_s(y_{k-1})$ actually coincides with $x_k$. Summing of $(k-1)/(k+r-2)\times\eqref{eq:prox_ineq}$ with $x=x_{k-1}, y = y_{k-1}$ and $(r-1)/(k+r-2)\times\eqref{eq:prox_ineq}$ with $x=x^\star, y=y_{k-1}$ gives \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} f(x_k) &\le \frac{k-1}{k+r-2}f(x_{k-1}) + \frac{r-1}{k+r-2}f^\star\\ & + \frac{r-1}{k+r-2}G_s(y_{k-1})^T\Big{(}\frac{k+r-2}{r-1}y_{k-1}-\frac{k-1}{r-1}x_{k-1} - x^\star\Big{)} - \frac{s}{2}\|G_s(y_{k-1})\|^2\\ &= \frac{k-1}{k+r-2}f(x_{k-1}) + \frac{r-1}{k+r-2}f^\star + \frac{(r-1)^2}{2s(k+r-2)^2}\Big{(}\|z_{k-1}-x^\star\|^2 - \|z_{k}-x^\star\|^2\Big{)}, \\ \end{aligned} \end{equation} where we use $z_{k-1}-s(k+r-2)G_s(y_{k-1})/(r-1)=z_{k}$. Rearranging the above inequality and multiplying by $2s(k+r-2)^2/(r-1)$ gives the desired \eqref{eq:recursive}.

nodes.name: Base case $2<lpha\le 4$
nodes.statement: First, consider $2 < \alpha \le 4$. Applying Theorem \ref{thm:large_r}, from \eqref{eq:bound_tilde_energy} we get that $\mathcal{E}(t)$ is upper bounded by \begin{equation} \mathcal{E}(t_{\alpha}) + \frac{(\alpha-2)(r-1)^2(2r-\alpha)\|x_0-x^\star\|^2}{8\mu t^{4-\alpha}} \le \mathcal{E}(t_{\alpha}) + \frac{(\alpha-2)(r-1)^2(2r-\alpha)\|x_0-x^\star\|^2}{8\mu t_{\alpha}^{4-\alpha}}. \end{equation} Then, we bound $\mathcal{E}(t_{\alpha})$ as follows. \begin{multline} \mathcal{E}(t_{\alpha}) \le t_{\alpha}^{\alpha}(f(X(t_{\alpha})) - f^\star) + \frac{(2r-\alpha)^2t_{\alpha}^{\alpha-2}}{4}\Big{\|}\frac{2r-2}{2r-\alpha}X(t_{\alpha})+ \frac{2t_{\alpha}}{2r-\alpha}\dot X(t_{\alpha}) - \frac{2r-2}{2r-\alpha}x^\star\Big{\|}^2\\ + \frac{(2r-\alpha)^2t_{\alpha}^{\alpha-2}}{4}\Big{\|}\frac{\alpha-2}{2r-\alpha}X(t_{\alpha})  - \frac{\alpha-2}{2r-\alpha}x^\star\Big{\|}^2 \\ \le (r-1)^2t_{\alpha}^{\alpha-2}\|x_0-x^\star\|^2 + \frac{(\alpha-2)^2(r-1)^2\|x_0-x^\star\|^2}{4\mu t_{\alpha}^{4-\alpha}}, \end{multline} where in the second inequality we use the decreasing property of the energy functional defined for Theorem \ref{thm:large_r}. Combining \eqref{eq:simple_bound_tilde_energy} and \eqref{eq:general_alpha_bound}, we have \begin{equation} \mathcal{E}(t) \le (r-1)^2t_{\alpha}^{\alpha-2}\|x_0-x^\star\|^2 + \frac{(\alpha-2)(r-1)^2(2r+\alpha-4)\|x_0-x^\star\|^2}{8\mu t_{\alpha}^{4-\alpha}} = O \Big{(} \frac{\|x_0-x^\star\|^2}{\mu^{\frac{\alpha-2}{2}}}  \Big{)}. \end{equation} For $t \ge t_{\alpha}$, it suffices to apply $f(X(t))-f^\star\le \mathcal{E}(t)/t^3$ to the last display. For $t < t_{\alpha}$, by Theorem \ref{thm:large_r}, $f(X(t)) - f^\star$ is upper bounded by \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \frac{(r-1)^2\|x_0 - x^\star\|^2}{2t^2} &\le \frac{(r-1)^2\mu^{\frac{\alpha-2}{2}}[(\alpha-2)(2r-\alpha)/(2\mu)]^{\frac{\alpha-2}{2}}}{2}\frac{\|x_0-x^\star\|^2}{\mu^{\frac{\alpha-2}{2}}t^{\alpha}} \\ &= O\Big{(}\frac{\|x_0-x^\star\|^2}{\mu^{\frac{\alpha-2}{2}}t^{\alpha}} \Big{)}. \end{aligned} \end{equation}

nodes.name: Inductive step $\alpha:=\tilde\alpha+1$
nodes.statement: Next, suppose that the theorem is valid for some $\tilde{\alpha} > 2$. We show below that this theorem is still valid for $\alpha := \tilde{\alpha} + 1$ if still $r \geq 3\alpha/2$. By the assumption, \eqref{eq:bound_tilde_energy} further induces \begin{equation} \mathcal{E}(t) \le \mathcal{E}(t_{\alpha}) + \frac{(\alpha-2)(2r-\alpha)t^{\alpha-2}}{4\mu}\frac{\tilde{C}\|x_0 - x^\star\|^2}{\mu^{\frac{\tilde{\alpha}-2}{2}}t^{\tilde{\alpha}}} \le \mathcal{E}(t_{\alpha}) + \frac{\tilde{C}(\alpha-2)(2r-\alpha)\|x_0 - x^\star\|^2}{4\mu^{\frac{\alpha-1}{2}}t_{\alpha}} \end{equation} for some constant $\tilde C$ only depending on $\tilde{\alpha}$ and $r$. This inequality with \eqref{eq:general_alpha_bound} implies \begin{align*} \mathcal{E}(t)  &\le (r-1)^2t_{\alpha}^{\alpha-2}\|x_0-x^\star\|^2 + \frac{(\alpha-2)^2(r-1)^2\|x_0-x^\star\|^2}{4\mu t_{\alpha}^{4-\alpha}} + \frac{\tilde{C}(\alpha-2)(2r-\alpha)\|x_0 - x^\star\|^2}{4\mu^{\frac{\alpha-1}{2}}t_{\alpha}} \\ &= O\left( \|x_0-x^\star\|^2/\mu^{\frac{\alpha-2}{2}} \right), \end{align*} which verify the induction for $t \geq t_{\alpha}$. As for $t < t_{\alpha}$, the validity of the induction follows from Theorem \ref{thm:large_r}, similarly to \eqref{eq:alpha_general_alpha_small_t}. Thus, combining the base and induction steps, the proof is completed.

nodes.name: Limit solves the ODE
First initial condition $ reve X(0)=x_0$
nodes.statement: The first condition $\breve X(0)= x_0$ is a direct consequence of $X_{\delta_{m_i}}(0) = x_0$.

nodes.name: Second initial condition (vanishing velocity)
Bound $a_k$ for $k\le\delta/\sqrt{s}$
nodes.statement: Let $z_k = (x_{k+1} - x_k)/\sqrt{s}$. Then Nesterov's scheme is equivalent to \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} x_{k+1} &= x_k + \sqrt{s}z_k\\ z_{k+1} & = \Big( 1 - \frac3{k+3} \Big) z_k - \sqrt{s}\nabla f\Big( x_k + \frac{2k+3}{k+3}\sqrt{s}z_k\Big). \end{aligned} \end{equation} Denote by $a_k = \|X_k^{\delta} - x_k\|, \quad b_k = \|Z_k^{\delta} - z_k\|$, whose initial values are $a_0 = 0$ and $b_0 = \|\nabla f(x_0)\|\sqrt{s}$. The idea of this proof is to bound $a_k$ via simultaneously estimating $a_k$ and $b_k$. By comparing \eqref{eq:euler_x_z} and \eqref{eq:nesterov_x_z}, we get the iterative relationship for $a_k$: $a_{k+1} \le a_k + \sqrt{s}b_k$. Denoting by $S_k = b_0 + b_1 + \cdots + b_k$, this yields \begin{equation} a_k \le \sqrt{s}S_{k-1}. \end{equation} By induction on $k$, for $k \le \delta/\sqrt{s}$ it holds that \[ b_k \le \frac{C_1Ls + C_2 + (C_1+C_2)\sqrt{Ls}}{2\sqrt{L}}(1 + \sqrt{Ls})^{k-1} - \frac{C_1Ls + C_2 - (C_1+C_2)\sqrt{Ls}}{2\sqrt{L}}(1 - \sqrt{Ls})^{k-1}. \] Letting $k^\star = \lfloor \delta/\sqrt{s} \rfloor$, we get \[ \limsup_{s \goto 0} \sqrt{s}S_{k^\star-1} \le \frac{C_2\e{\delta\sqrt{L}} + C_2 \e{-\delta\sqrt{L}} - 2C_2}{2L} = O(\delta^2), \] which allows us to conclude that \begin{equation} a_k \le \sqrt{s}S_{k-1} = O(\delta^2) + o_s(1) \end{equation} for all $k \le \delta/\sqrt{s}$.

nodes.name: Bound $b_k$ for $k>k^\star$ and combine
nodes.statement: Next, we bound $b_k$ for $k > k^\star = \lfloor \delta/\sqrt{s} \rfloor$. To this end, we consider the worst case of \eqref{eq:bk_iterative}, that is, \[ b_{k+1} = b_k + LsS_{k-1} + \frac{C_2s}{\delta} \] for $k > k^\star$ and $S_{k^\star} = S_{k^\star+1} = C_3\delta^2/\sqrt{s} + o_s(1/\sqrt{s})$ for some sufficiently large $C_3$. In this case, $C_2s/\delta < sS_{k-1}$ for sufficiently small $s$. Hence, the last display gives \[ b_{k+1} \le b_k + (L+1)sS_{k-1}. \] By induction, we get \[ S_k \le \frac{C_3\delta^2/\sqrt{s} + o_s(1/\sqrt{s})}{2}\left( (1+\sqrt{(L+1)s})^{k-k^\star} +  (1-\sqrt{(L+1)s})^{k-k^\star} \right). \] Letting $k^\diamond = \lfloor T/\sqrt{s} \rfloor$, we further get \[ \limsup_{s\goto 0} \sqrt{s}S_{k^\diamond} \le \frac{C_3\delta^2(\e{(T-\delta)\sqrt{L+1}} + \e{-(T-\delta)\sqrt{L+1}})}{2} = O(\delta^2), \] which yields \begin{equation} a_k \le \sqrt{s}S_{k-1} = O(\delta^2) + o_s(1) \end{equation} for $k^\star < k \le k^\diamond$. Last, combining \eqref{eq:ak_bound_delta} and the last display, we get the desired result.

nodes.name: Input
nodes.statement: \STATE \textbf{input:} $x_0\in\R^n, y_0 = x_0, x_{-1} = x_0, 0 < s \le 1/L, k_{\max}\in\mathbb{N}^+$ and $k_{\min}\in\mathbb{N}^+$

nodes.name: Initialize counter $j$
nodes.statement: \STATE $j \gets 1$

nodes.name: Main loop over $k$
nodes.statement: \FOR{$k = 1$ to $k_{\max}$}

nodes.name: Proximal gradient update of $x_k$
nodes.statement: \STATE $x_k \gets \mbox{argmin}_x(\frac{1}{2s}\|x - y_{k-1} + s\nabla g(y_{k-1})\|^2 + h(x))$

nodes.name: Momentum update of $y_k$
nodes.statement: \STATE $y_k \gets x_k + \frac{j-1}{j+2}(x_k - x_{k-1})$

nodes.name: Speed restarting branch
nodes.statement: \IF{ $\|x_k - x_{k-1}\| < \|x_{k-1} - x_{k-2}\|$ {\bf{and}} $j \ge k_{\min}$} \STATE $j \gets 1$ \ELSE \STATE $j \gets j + 1$ \ENDIF
